extracted.intended_audience: writers of scientific hoaxes/speculative fiction, editors, and literary critics interested in plausibility
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criticism for composing scientifically-plausible speculative/hoax fiction (here, lunar/astronomical hoaxes), emphasizing factual accuracy, internal consistency, and originality when using scientific detail to lend plausibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scrupulous attention to facts and general analogy
rubrics_metrics.description: The fiction should observe facts and general analogy closely; scientific detail used to lend plausibility must be accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the text: 'it wanted much of the force which might have been given it by a more scrupulous attention to facts and to general analogy.' Use scientific detail to give plausibility, but verify facts; sloppy or contradictory facts weaken the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate physical and optical calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical quantities and optical powers invoked (distances, magnifications, angular sizes) must be internally consistent and within real-world limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example/anti-pattern in the notes: Mr. L. makes his lens have a power of 42,000 times; dividing the moon's distance by that power gives an apparent distance of about five miles—making detailed observation of minute objects impossible. Verify numerical claims (e.g., 'By this divide 240,000... and we have five miles and five sevenths, as the apparent distance'). Don't claim visibility of objects smaller than the optical system permits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check factual claims about real persons/institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements that invoke real manufacturers, establishments, or historical facts should be checked for basic truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: attributing molding of a prodigious glass to 'Messrs. Hartley and Grant, in Dumbarton' when that establishment had 'ceased operations for many years previous to the publication of the hoax.' Such claims invite refutation and undermine the hoax/fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of biological/ecological reasoning with astronomical conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Biological adaptations and ecological descriptions must align with the described illumination and environmental conditions of the setting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: the note objects to reasoning that a 'hairy veil' protects lunar animals from 'great extremes of light and darkness' because 'the inhabitants of our side of the moon have, evidently, no darkness at all' (they receive light from the Earth). Account for actual lighting regimes, atmospheres, and their consequences for lifeforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topographical and cartographic consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions of geography/topography should be consistent with known charts/maps and with the work's own internal geography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notes state 'The topography throughout... is entirely at variance with that or any other lunar chart, and even grossly at variance with itself.' If referencing existing charts (real or fictional), ensure alignment or explicitly explain departures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct use of compass points and coordinate conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: When invoking directional terminology or maps, use appropriate conventions for the celestial/body-specific context (e.g., lunar maps differ from terrestrial maps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern cited: 'The points of the compass, too, are in inextricable confusion; the writer appearing to be ignorant that, on a lunar map, these are not in accordance with terrestrial points; the east being to the left, etc.' Learn and apply the correct orientation rules for the setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect domain-specific terminology and implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialized terms (e.g., 'Mare') carry field-specific meanings and implications; do not treat them as if they imply terrestrial analogues unless justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notes criticize treating 'Mare Nubium, Mare Tranquillitatis' as oceans—'whereas there is no astronomical point more positively ascertained than that no such bodies exist there.' Know the technical meanings before extrapolating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical consequences must follow from material properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical descriptions (e.g., appearance of a terminator, reflections, surface behavior) must follow from the material properties asserted (liquid vs solid, surface roughness, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'In examining the boundary between light and darkness... the line of division is found to be rough and jagged; but, were these dark places liquid, it would evidently be even.' If you describe liquid surfaces, ensure accompanying optical/visual consequences are consistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and avoidance of uncredited copying
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions or wonderful inventions should not be literal copies of prior published imagery or passages; maintain originality or attribute clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notes point out: 'The description of the wings of the man-bat... is but a literal copy of Peter Wilkins' account.' Literal copying undermines credibility and artistic merit; avoid plagiarism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not depend solely on audience ignorance to succeed
rubrics_metrics.description: Relying on public ignorance to sustain a hoax is risky; knowledgeable readers will expose basic errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author comments that the public were misled only because of 'the gross ignorance... upon subjects of an astronomical nature.' If the goal is plausibility rather than deception, ensure claims can withstand scrutiny by informed readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use scientific detail to lend plausibility—but verify it
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific detail is a powerful device to make fiction plausible, but it must be used accurately and consistently to strengthen rather than weaken the tale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct quote context: 'both attempt to give plausibility by scientific detail'—this is a recommended technique, provided the underlying facts and analogies are correct; careless science will have the opposite effect.
